The failing test `testContainsIgnoreCase_LocaleIndependence` in `StringUtilsEqualsIndexOfTest` class from Apache Commons Lang library is testing the `containsIgnoreCase` method. 

The current bug report mentions an issue related to case-insensitive string handling and highlights that `String.to*Case()` being locale-sensitive is usually not intended for case-insensitive comparisons.

Looking at the implementation of the `containsIgnoreCase` method in `StringUtils` class, we can see that it converts strings to uppercase using `str.toUpperCase()` before performing the comparison. This means that the method is using the default locale for case-insensitive comparison, which can lead to unexpected behavior as highlighted in the bug report.

To fix this issue and make the case-insensitive comparison locale-independent, developers should consider using methods like `StringUtils.lowerCase(String, Locale)` and `StringUtils.upperCase(String, Locale)` that allow specifying a fixed locale for case transformation. 

Therefore, the root cause of the bug is the incorrect handling of case-insensitive comparison without considering locale sensitivity in the `containsIgnoreCase` method of `StringUtils` class.

Next, I will suggest the methods that should be fixed to address this issue.
```
org.apache.commons.lang.StringUtils.containsIgnoreCase(java.lang.String, java.lang.String)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
